USB connector **shape** and USB **capability** are different questions.

::: {.tej-image-hero}
![USB Type-A, Type-B, Micro-B, Mini-B, and Type-C connector shapes.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/USB_A%2C_B%2C_C_%281.1-3.0%29_connectors.svg)
:::

*Figure 1. Common USB shapes. [Open image source and licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:USB_A,_B,_C_(1.1-3.0)_connectors.svg)*

:::: {.tej-visual-grid}
::: {.tej-visual-card}
### USB Type-A

The familiar rectangular connector for computers, chargers, flash drives, mice, and keyboards.
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
### USB Type-B

The square connector still used on printers, audio interfaces, and lab devices.
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
### Mini-USB and Micro-USB

Older small connectors on cameras, controllers, phones, and embedded boards.
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
### USB-C

Small and reversible. It may carry data, charging, docks, storage, Ethernet, audio, or video, but not every cable supports every feature.
:::
::::

## USB-C cables are different

:::: {.tej-visual-grid}
::: {.tej-visual-card}
![USB-C port beside a matching USB-C cable plug.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/OnePlus_3_USB_port_and_the_cable.jpg)

### USB-C to USB-C

Check the printed specification for data speed, charging power, and video support.

*Figure 2. [Open source and licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:OnePlus_3_USB_port_and_the_cable.jpg)*
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
![USB Type-A to USB-C cable.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:Redirect/file/USB_3.1_Gen2_Typ-C_to_Typ-A_cable_10Gbps_PD_60W.jpg)

### USB-A to USB-C

A passive A-to-C cable does **not** carry DisplayPort Alt Mode to a monitor. An active USB graphics dock is different: it contains electronics and usually needs a driver.

*Figure 3. [Open source and licence.](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:USB_3.1_Gen2_Typ-C_to_Typ-A_cable_10Gbps_PD_60W.jpg)*
:::
::::

### Check four things

1. Connector shape at each end.
2. Data speed printed on the cable or package.
3. Maximum charging power in watts.
4. Explicit DisplayPort, USB4, or Thunderbolt support when video is needed.

## Common peripherals

:::: {.tej-visual-grid}
::: {.tej-visual-card}
### Mouse and keyboard

USB-A, USB-C, Bluetooth, or a small wireless receiver.
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
### Headphones and microphone

3.5 mm audio, USB-A, USB-C, or Bluetooth.
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
### Storage and printers

Flash drive, HDD, SSD, card reader, printer, scanner, or camera.
:::

::: {.tej-visual-card}
### Controllers

Webcam, game controller, drawing tablet, robotics controller, or microcontroller.
:::
::::

## Clean cable management

:::: {.tej-path-strip}
<div><strong>BACK</strong>Fixed cables: power, monitor, Ethernet, keyboard, mouse</div>
<div><strong>EDGE</strong>Route with gentle bends and hook-and-loop straps</div>
<div><strong>CLEAR</strong>Keep vents, feet, chair wheels, and walkways free</div>
::::

Leave a small service loop. Label both ends of similar cables. Do not pull tight, crush under furniture, or hang weight from a connector.

**Visual check:** photograph the back of one correctly connected computer. Label power, monitor signal, Ethernet, keyboard, mouse, audio, and one spare USB port.
